- When sentiment is consistently positive (≥0.67) over recent days, model tends to overestimate prices; reduce forecast by 1–3% for next period.
- After a sharp price spike (e.g., >+5% from prior period), model often overshoots; cap forecast at +3% above prior peak or use 2-period moving average for smoothing.
- If sentiment turns negative (≤0.33) within 3–5 days, model frequently fails to adjust downward; apply downward bias of 1–2% per negative sentiment day.
- Mean reversion is strong in 3–5 day horizon; if forecast is >+5% above recent 10-day average, reduce by 1–2% per day until convergence.
- For 30-day forecasts, model often overestimates early in the horizon (first 5–7 days); apply linear decay correction: reduce forecast by 0.5–1% per day after day 5.
- If sentiment history shows alternating highs/lows (e.g., +0.67, -0.33, +0.67), model tends to misread momentum; use sentiment-weighted average of last 3–5 days for smoothing.
